guide.dashboard.history: Every transform with its cost, plus a preview of the last one.
guide.dashboard.logs: Redacted app events, searchable and exportable.

guide.intro: FixLang lives in your menu bar. Select text in any app, press a shortcut, and an AI model rewrites it — fixing grammar, summarizing, translating, or whatever the preset asks for.
guide.loadError: Could not read your current setup. The steps below still apply.
guide.output.heading: What happens to the result
guide.output.unknown: Set in Settings → General → Transform output.
guide.presets.empty: No presets yet. Add one in Settings → Transform.
guide.presets.heading: Your preset shortcuts
guide.privacy.body: History, logs and keys are stored on this Mac. Keys are encrypted with the macOS keychain and are never shown to the interface again after you save them. Requests go only to the providers you connect, each carrying only its own key.
guide.privacy.title: What stays on your Mac
guide.records.body: Two Settings → General controls decide whether History and Usage show anything. Connect a provider (API key or local server) so transforms run and History fills. Add an Admin / Provisioning key when you want the Usage tab to show account-level spend.
guide.records.title: What happened to the records?
guide.result.body: Every transform is saved to History with its cost and a preview of the output. With Direct paste, FixLang replaces your selection as soon as the model finishes. With Show popup, the result opens in a small dialog so you can read or copy it before the source text changes.
guide.result.example.text: This is an example of the popup result. Your corrected text would appear here while the original selection stays unchanged until you close or copy it.
guide.result.title: What happens to the result?
guide.setup.model.body: Settings → General → Default model. Every preset uses it unless the preset names a model of its own.
guide.setup.model.title: Pick a default model
guide.setup.permission.body: macOS asks the first time you press a shortcut. FixLang needs it to read the selected text and paste the result back.
guide.setup.permission.title: Allow Accessibility access
guide.setup.provider.body: Settings → General → Providers. Add an API key for OpenAI or OpenRouter, or point FixLang at a local Ollama or LM Studio server, then press Connect.
guide.setup.provider.none: No provider is connected yet — a transform cannot run until one is.
guide.setup.provider.title: Connect a provider
guide.setup.title: Set up once
guide.title: Getting started
guide.topic.adminKey.body: Optional. Add an OpenAI admin key or an OpenRouter provisioning key to fill the Usage tab with account-level spend.
guide.topic.adminKey.title: Admin / Provisioning keys
guide.topic.combo.body: Chain 2–5 presets behind one hotkey in Settings → Correction, feeding each result into the next. Press Control+Escape while it runs to cancel before anything is delivered.
guide.topic.combo.title: Combos
guide.topic.guards.body: FixLang checks four things before your selection leaves this machine: whether the frontmost app is on your blocked list, whether the text looks older than the clipboard age limit, whether it is longer than the size limit, and whether it contains anything shaped like a credential. Three of them ask before sending rather than refusing outright. All four are adjustable, and each can be turned off. The Security dashboard tab shows what they have actually done.
guide.topic.guards.title: Guards before text is sent
guide.topic.language.body: The interface follows your system language on first run. Change it in Settings → General; every window updates without a restart.
guide.topic.language.title: Language
guide.topic.models.body: Give a preset its own model when it needs more capability than your default, and leave the others inheriting that default.
guide.topic.models.title: Model per preset
guide.topic.output.body: Choose Show popup when you want to read the result before it replaces your text, and Direct paste when you trust it to land straight in the document.
guide.topic.output.title: Transform output
guide.topic.presets.body: Each preset carries its own system prompt and shortcut. Edit one when the wording is off, or add a preset for a job the built-ins do not cover.
guide.topic.presets.title: Preset prompt
guide.topic.profiles.body: A profile holds its own providers, presets and history — one for work, one for personal writing. Press {hotkey} to switch to the next one.
guide.topic.profiles.title: Profiles
guide.topic.promptGen.body: Press {hotkey} on a selection to build a full AI prompt from it.
guide.topic.promptGen.title: Prompt generator
guide.topic.theme.body: Settings → Appearance holds the bundled terminal-inspired themes. A change applies instantly in every window.
guide.topic.theme.title: Theme
guide.topics.title: Settings worth knowing

guide.transform.press: Press the shortcut of the preset you want.
guide.transform.receive: FixLang sends the text, then pastes the result back or shows it in a popup.

security.clipboardAge.description: While this is on, FixLang checks the clipboard once a second in the background. It stores only a fingerprint and a timestamp — never the text. Set to 0 to turn this off.
security.clipboardAge.disabledHint: 0 disables this guard and stops the background check entirely.
security.clipboardAge.title: Stale clipboard
security.deniedApps.description: Transforms are refused while one of these apps is frontmost. The selection is still copied and restored — it just never reaches a provider.
security.deniedApps.title: Blocked apps
security.restorePartial.guardFailed: Restore only partly worked — the blocked apps, clipboard age and selection size settings failed to save and were left unchanged. The secret guard settings were restored.
security.restorePartial.secretFailed: Restore only partly worked — the secret guard settings failed to save and were left unchanged. The other settings were restored.
security.secretGuard.description: Scans text before it's sent for things that look like API keys, tokens, or passwords.
security.secretGuard.highEntropy.hint: Catches secrets with no recognizable prefix, at the cost of more false positives.
security.secretGuard.highEntropy.label: Flag random-looking strings
security.secretGuard.limitations.body: This is a pattern check, not a guarantee. It looks for the shapes credentials usually have, and will miss a secret that does not look like one. It will sometimes flag things that are not secrets. In Mask and restore mode, a value it recognizes but cannot cover completely is never masked in part: the whole request falls back to the confirm dialog instead, and choosing Send anyway there sends every secret in that selection in full — including ones that would have been masked on their own. It only checks text FixLang is about to send — it does not watch your clipboard contents, your screen, or what you type elsewhere. It cannot un-send. Text you send is saved to your local history on this machine, including when you choose Send anyway. Inline autocomplete cannot ask you anything — it fires while you type — so it simply does not send a suggestion request when this check matches the text around your caret or the context attached to your question. That still cannot protect a credential you are part-way through typing, because earlier keystrokes have already been sent.
security.secretGuard.limitations.title: What this can and can't do
security.secretGuard.maskHint: Masking replaces the values it recognizes before your text is sent. A secret it doesn't recognize is sent just as it would be with the guard off, and a value it can't cover completely asks you first instead.
security.secretGuard.mode.label: Mode
security.secretGuard.title: Secret guard
security.selectionSize.description: Selections longer than this ask for confirmation before they're sent.
security.selectionSize.disabledHint: 0 disables this guard — every selection is sent without asking.
security.selectionSize.title: Large selections
security.stats.askContextDropped.hint: Ask ran without the selection attached because a guard fired on it. The question itself was still sent.
security.stats.askContextDropped.label: Ask context dropped
security.stats.blockedByApp.hint: The frontmost app was on your blocked list, so nothing was sent.
security.stats.blockedByApp.label: Blocked by app
security.stats.declinedLargeSelection.hi: You cancelled at the size confirmation.
security.stats.declinedStaleClipboard.hi: You cancelled after being told the selection looked older than the age limit.
security.stats.declinedUnknownClipboardA: You cancelled when the age of the text couldn't be established — usually just after FixLang started.
security.stats.empty: No guard has fired in this range — nothing was blocked, masked, or confirmed.
security.stats.footnote: Counted from this machine's local logs, so clearing the Logs tab resets these numbers. Only interventions are recorded: a guard that lets text through writes nothing, so there is no total to compare these against.
security.stats.restoreFailures.hint: The reply came back without its placeholders, so it opened in a popup instead of being pasted.
security.stats.restoreFailures.label: Values not restored
security.stats.rules.hint: Which detectors matched. Counted once per request, not once per value.
